title: Mathematics — latest arXiv batch (15 Oct 2026): 7 notable papers
global_caveat: This is an inferred selection of notable recent work, not a measured hottest ranking: arXiv supplies no official trending chart, the submissions are about a day old, citation totals were unavailable in the snapshot, and no independent discussion signal was verified.

sections.title: The existence of small defining polynomials for number fields
sections.abstract: Every degree-n number field of absolute discriminant D has a defining integral polynomial whose coefficients are O_n(√D), resolving Ruppert’s 1998 conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove the coefficient-height bound and resolve the conjecture without assuming the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Degree n and discriminant D are fixed parameters; the implied constant may depend on n.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an arXiv preprint; the bound is not uniform in the degree.

sections.title: Proof of the Penrose Conjecture for Maximally Parameterized Initial Data Sets
sections.abstract: For a specified class of asymptotically flat initial data in every dimension n ≥ 3, the authors prove a spacetime Penrose inequality by constructing a nonnegative-scalar-curvature comparison metric.
sections.claimed_result: The theorem obtains the ADM-energy Penrose bound for maximally parameterized data when the comparison metric has the stated horizon completion, asymptotic flatness, and matching ADM energy.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The data must satisfy the dominant energy condition and admit the paper’s maximally parameterized form; the comparison metric must complete smoothly to a minimal boundary and meet the theorem’s asymptotic hypotheses.
sections.unique_caveat: This does not prove the unrestricted spacetime Penrose conjecture. The authors identify general existence for their degenerate PDE system as a remaining problem.

sections.title: Supercritical sharpness for Ising double random currents
sections.abstract: In dimensions d ≥ 3 and above the critical inverse temperature, the double-random-current percolation model has local uniqueness of its macroscopic cluster with high probability, uniformly over source boundary conditions.
sections.claimed_result: The authors derive local uniqueness and use it to recover exponential decay of truncated Ising correlations and exponential mixing for the FK-Ising measure.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The principal theorem is for the nearest-neighbour Ising model on ℤᵈ with d ≥ 3 and β > βc, uniformly over even source sets.
sections.unique_caveat: The two stated exponential-decay/mixing consequences were previously established; the paper’s claimed advance there is a simpler proof. Its principal theorem is stated for d ≥ 3.

sections.title: Effective equidistribution of polynomial trajectories in SL₃(ℝ)/SL₃(ℤ)
sections.abstract: For a fixed matrix-polynomial trajectory, the authors give a necessary-and-sufficient Diophantine criterion for power-rate equidistribution on its homogeneous orbit closure, using polynomial tests of degree at most two.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves the degree-two test bound is optimal in general and establishes effective equidistribution under the intrinsic criterion.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The result concerns a fixed polynomial curve in SL₃(ℝ)/SL₃(ℤ), its homogeneous orbit closure, and time averages against smooth compactly supported test functions.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a criterion for a fixed trajectory, not a guarantee that every polynomial trajectory satisfies the required Diophantine condition.

sections.title: Arithmetic Siegel–Weil formula on the product of modular curves
sections.abstract: The authors prove the full generating-series arithmetic Siegel–Weil formula on a product of two modular curves, including arbitrarily singular coefficients; this is the GSpin(2,2) case of Kudla’s program.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish the arithmetic generating-series identity for the product of two modular curves, treating coefficients arising from singular matrices.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The stated setting is the product of two modular curves, corresponding to the split GSpin(2,2) case.
sections.unique_caveat: This is one specific low-dimensional case of Kudla’s program, not a general formula for higher-dimensional Shimura varieties.

sections.title: Hypergraphs with the smallest Hall ratio are still hard to colour
sections.abstract: For every uniformity k ≥ 3, the authors construct k-uniform hypergraphs with the minimum possible Hall ratio k/(k−1) but arbitrarily large fractional chromatic number.
sections.claimed_result: The authors show that at every k ≥ 3 the Hall ratio can be exactly minimal while the fractional chromatic number is unbounded; this also forces unbounded ordinary chromatic number.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The result concerns k-uniform hypergraphs for fixed k ≥ 3; the paper distinguishes fractional chromatic number from ordinary chromatic number.
sections.unique_caveat: The separation is a hypergraph phenomenon and does not carry over to graphs (k = 2), where the minimum Hall ratio forces 2-colourability.

sections.title: Fast separation of Euler and Navier–Stokes flows in two dimensions
sections.abstract: The authors construct a stationary two-dimensional Euler solution for which a Navier–Stokes solution with the same initial datum separates on a time scale proportional to log(1/ν), where ν is viscosity.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim the fastest separation from Euler steady states, with logarithmic-in-inverse-viscosity time scale.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The paper studies two-dimensional incompressible flows on the torus, initialized from the constructed stationary Euler solution.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an existence construction for a particular steady initial flow; it does not say that typical Euler/Navier–Stokes pairs separate at this rate.
